sections.h2: What does the Eaton County Register of Deeds actually do?
sections.html:
Eaton County's register keeps the county's land title file: deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and any other paper that touches real estate between Charlotte, Grand Ledge, Eaton Rapids and the townships around them. Each filing is checked against Michigan's recording rules and then stored as a digital image.

Nobody at the counter will write a deed for you. The county page puts responsibility for wording and purpose on the person who prepared the paper, and it sends legal questions to an attorney. If a deed still has to be written, a title company or real estate lawyer can do it, and the signed original comes here afterward.

The counter opens at 8:30 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, with the staff away from noon until 1:00. Courthouse holidays interrupt that schedule, as the notice about Veterans Day on the register's page shows. Anything sent by mail should include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, because the office requires one before it sends documents back.

sections.h2: What does it cost to file papers in Charlotte?
sections.html:
A flat $30 covers each deed, mortgage, lis pendens or certified real estate copy. The extras are itemized on the county's fees page.

Eaton County register charges, copied from the posted schedule
ItemCharge
Filing one deed, mortgage or similar paper$30
Each further instrument that one paper assigns or discharges$3 each
Tax certificate, first 25 legal descriptions$5
Each description past that$0.20
Ordinary copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2 a page
Certified copy of a recorded document$1 a page plus $5 for the seal

The website does not sell certified copies. Ask at the counter or write to the office.

sections.h2: When does a deed need the treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, a land contract or an assignment of one cannot go on the record until the county treasurer's office has certified the parcel. The county cites MCL 211.135, which wants proof that nobody holds a tax lien or tax title on the land and that five years of taxes before the instrument date are settled.

The statute excuses quitclaim deeds and other conveyances without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds. Closers usually order the certificate while escrow is open, so sellers seldom chase it themselves.

  • The treasurer's certificate stapled to a warranty deed or land contract.
  • The full price printed on the deed, or a value affidavit attached.
  • An addressed envelope with postage when the package travels by mail.
  • The $30 filing charge plus $5 for the certificate where one is required.

Incomplete packages return to the sender, which can delay a closing by days. A parcel with unpaid taxes does not get a clean certificate until the balance is cleared.

sections.h2: How much Michigan transfer tax does an Eaton County seller owe?
sections.html:
Two levies attach to the deed. The state's is $3.75 on every $500 slice of price (MCL 207.525). The county's is 55 cents on each slice, the rate for counties below two million residents (MCL 207.504). A fraction of a slice counts as a whole one.

Both fall on the grantor (MCL 207.502 and 207.523). The treasurer must receive the state portion within 15 days of the deed changing hands.

A sale at $216,900, the median value QuickFacts reports for Eaton County, works out to 434 slices. That means $1,627.50 to the state and $238.70 to the county, $1,866.20 in all. A purchase contract can push the cost onto the buyer, yet the statute still names the seller.

sections.h2: Which Eaton County transfers owe nothing?
sections.html:
Michigan excuses many transfers, as long as the instrument says which exemption applies. The county list is MCL 207.505 and the state list is MCL 207.526. Most entries match, apart from the family item at the end.

  • Price below $100.
  • Mortgages and other security papers, with their assignments and discharges.
  • Leases and leasehold transfers.
  • Court orders that move title without naming a price.
  • Quitclaim deeds fixing a flaw in title the grantee already holds.
  • Land contracts until legal title actually passes.
  • State tax only: a gift deed running from parent to child or stepchild, or grandparent to grandchild.

If tax was paid on a deal that qualified, MCL 207.523(4) lets the seller, or a buyer who paid in the seller's place, ask the state Department of Treasury for the money back.

sections.h2: How far back can you search Eaton County land records?
sections.html:
The search link on the register's page reaches every record from 1836 up to the most recent proof date, so a whole chain of title can be traced from home. A link for electronic filing sits beside it.

Electronic filing lets a title company submit the signed deed the same day with no courier. Ask your closer whether the file goes in that way and when the recorded copy will reach you. Money owed on a parcel is a separate matter, and the county treasurer runs its own search for it.

sections.h2: What is the Eaton County landscape like?
sections.html:
Eaton County covers 579 square miles, 575 of them land, beside Ingham County, and part of the city of Lansing falls inside its lines. Lawmakers organized it on December 29, 1837 and named it for John H. Eaton, a secretary of war under President Jackson. Charlotte holds the courthouse. Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet and Potterville are the other cities.

Interstates 69, 96 and 496 run through the county, joined by M-43, M-50 and M-99. Eleven school districts serve it, among them Charlotte, Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet, Potterville, Maple Valley, Bellevue and Waverly, and a few edges send children to schools in neighboring counties. The road commission looks after more than 1,170 miles of county roads, most of them outside city limits.

  • QuickFacts lists 109,581 residents as of July 2025 and 48,090 housing units.
  • About three in four homes are lived in by their owners, 74.2% to be exact.
  • Median household income is $79,597 across 45,428 households.
  • Half of renters pay at least $1,092 a month.

sections.h2: What happens when Eaton County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent bills are the county treasurer's job, and the same office is the foreclosing unit for parcels that stay behind. Its page says over 2,000 foreclosures have been prevented since 2016 and links a chart of Michigan's foreclosure deadlines.

Payment can be made online once the parcel number and amount are found in the county's tax search. A 2.49% fee applies to cards, and parcels inside Lansing use their own link. A county land bank deals with vacant and foreclosed property.

An owner in that spot can still sell. The payoff comes out of the sale money, and the treasurer's certificate tells the closer what must clear first.

faqs.q: Where is a deed filed in Eaton County?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds in Charlotte, the county seat. The register's page on eatoncounty.org gives the counter location. Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:30, except for the noon hour.

faqs.q: How much does Eaton County ask for a filing?
faqs.a: It is $30 for each document. An assignment or discharge that reaches several instruments adds $3 per extra instrument, and a tax certificate is $5 for 25 descriptions or fewer.

faqs.q: Can an Eaton County deed be filed online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the e-record link on the register's page. Paper filings by mail need a stamped envelope addressed back to the sender.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on an Eaton County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, by statute. A purchase agreement can assign the cost to the buyer. The state share reaches the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

faqs.q: How old are the records online?
faqs.a: They start in 1836 and run to the latest proof date. Certified copies are not sold on the website, so contact the register's office for those.
